## 4. DESIGN SYSTEM (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

> Every visual property in this project MUST come from the design token system.
> There are NO exceptions. A hardcoded `#333333` is a bug. A hardcoded `16px` is a bug.

**Token files:**
- Source of truth: `design-tokens/tokens.json`
- Web implementation: `design-tokens/tokens.css` (imported in global styles)
- Mobile implementation: `design-tokens/theme.dart`

**What tokens cover:**
- Colours (brand, semantic, surface, text, border)
- Typography (font family, size scale, weight, line-height, letter-spacing)
- Spacing (4px base grid — all spacing is multiples of 4)
- Border radius
- Shadows / elevation
- Animation duration and easing
- Breakpoints

**Adding a new visual property:**
1. Check if a token already exists for it
2. If not, propose the token addition to the human BEFORE using it
3. Never add a one-off value inline

**Component rules:**
- Use the component library before building a new component
- Component library location: `{{COMPONENT_LIBRARY_PATH}}`
- New components must use only tokens and must be added to the library
- No component-specific colour or spacing hardcoded in component files

## 5. NEVER DO LIST

These are absolute prohibitions. Not guidelines. Not suggestions. If you are about to do
any of the following, STOP and tell the human what you were going to do and why.

### Environment & Identity
- ❌ Never hardcode a Firebase project ID, app ID, or bucket name in application code
- ❌ Never hardcode a Vercel, Netlify, or Supabase project ID in scripts or configs
- ❌ Never use a production environment ID in local development or testing
- ❌ Never commit a secret, API key, token, or credential to git (even in a test file)
- ❌ Never add `.env` files to git — only `.env.example` with empty values
- ❌ Never create a new Firebase project, Vercel project, or cloud resource without explicit human instruction

### Code Quality
- ❌ Never leave a `TODO` without a corresponding entry in `docs/TECH_DEBT.md`
- ❌ Never use `any` type in TypeScript (use `unknown` and narrow it)
- ❌ Never disable an ESLint rule without a comment explaining why
- ❌ Never merge to `{{PRIMARY_BRANCH}}` without CI passing
- ❌ Never skip writing tests for business logic, auth flows, or payment code
- ❌ Never use `console.log` in production code (use the project logger)
- ❌ Never write code that only works on the developer's machine

### Design
- ❌ Never hardcode a colour, font size, spacing value, or border radius
- ❌ Never introduce a new font that isn't in the design token system
- ❌ Never create a one-off button, card, or input style — use or extend the component library
- ❌ Never implement a UI pattern that breaks on mobile (test all breakpoints)

### Architecture
- ❌ Never build a custom tool if an approved tool already exists (check `docs/TOOL_REGISTRY.md`)
- ❌ Never add a new npm/pub dependency without checking it is maintained, secure, and necessary
- ❌ Never make a breaking API change without an ADR documenting the decision
- ❌ Never store user PII in a place it isn't documented as being stored
- ❌ Never expose a server secret to the client bundle

### Agents Specifically
- ❌ Never assume which environment you are operating in — check the manifest
- ❌ Never assume a file hasn't changed since you last read it — re-read before editing
- ❌ Never make multiple file changes simultaneously without checking dependencies
- ❌ Never run a destructive command (drop table, delete bucket, purge cache) without explicit confirmation
- ❌ Never spawn a subagent from within a subagent — all delegation is orchestrator-only (see `MULTI_AGENT.md` → Subagent Contract, Element 4)
- ❌ Never spawn a subagent without specifying scope, `disallowedTools`, `maxTurns`, and isolation mode — uncontracted subagents are prohibited (see `MULTI_AGENT.md` → Subagent Contract)

## 6. ALWAYS DO LIST

### Before Writing Any Code
- ✅ Read the relevant section of this file
- ✅ Check `docs/scratchpad/DAILY.md` — if it exists and was modified today or
  yesterday, read it before starting. It contains recent operational learnings
  that may directly affect your task. Pay attention to entries marked `rule`.
- ✅ Check `docs/TOOL_REGISTRY.md` — does a tool already exist for this?
- ✅ Check the component library — does a component already exist for this?
- ✅ Confirm which environment you're operating in
- ✅ Run `git status` and understand the current state of the branch

### When Writing Code
- ✅ Write TypeScript (or Dart) with strict mode enabled
- ✅ Write tests alongside the code, not after
- ✅ Use only design tokens for visual properties
- ✅ Handle errors explicitly — never swallow exceptions silently
- ✅ Add JSDoc/DartDoc comments to exported functions and classes
- ✅ Consider mobile first — implement mobile layout before desktop

### When Finishing a Task
- ✅ Run the linter and fix all errors before considering the task complete
- ✅ Run the type checker — zero type errors is the standard
- ✅ Run tests — they must pass
- ✅ Check for console.logs and remove them
- ✅ Update `docs/TECH_DEBT.md` if you've made a compromise
- ✅ Write a meaningful commit message (format: `type(scope): description`)

### When Unsure
- ✅ Stop and ask the human — do not guess
- ✅ Prefer doing less and confirming over doing more and being wrong
- ✅ If you see an inconsistency between this file and the codebase, flag it

## 7. COMMIT MESSAGE FORMAT

```
type(scope): short description

Types: feat | fix | style | refactor | test | docs | chore | security | perf
Scope: the module/component/area affected

Examples:
  feat(auth): add Google OAuth sign-in flow
  fix(checkout): correct Stripe webhook signature validation
  style(tokens): add missing border-radius-lg token
  security(api): rate-limit password reset endpoint
  perf(images): migrate hero images to next/image with blur placeholder
```

---

## 8. BRANCH STRATEGY

```
main          → production-ready, protected, requires PR + CI pass
staging       → pre-production integration branch
feature/*     → new features, branch from main
fix/*         → bug fixes, branch from main
hotfix/*      → production emergency fixes, branch from main, merge to main + staging
chore/*       → maintenance, tooling, dependency updates
```

---

## 9. SECURITY RULES

Full detail in `SECURITY.md`. Mandatory highlights:

- All user input is validated server-side (client validation is UX only)
- Auth tokens are stored in httpOnly cookies, never localStorage
- All API routes validate authentication before processing
- Stripe webhook endpoints validate signature before processing payload
- Firebase Security Rules are reviewed on every deploy
- Supabase RLS (Row Level Security) is enabled on all tables
- No secrets in environment variables accessible to client bundle
- CORS is explicitly configured — no wildcard in production
- Content Security Policy headers are set on all pages
- Rate limiting is applied to all auth and payment endpoints

---

## 10. PERFORMANCE BUDGETS

These are measured in CI. A PR that regresses beyond these values requires human approval.

| Metric | Budget | Tool |
|--------|--------|------|
| Lighthouse Performance | ≥ 90 | Lighthouse CI |
| Lighthouse Accessibility | ≥ 95 | Lighthouse CI |
| First Contentful Paint | < 1.5s | Web Vitals |
| Largest Contentful Paint | < 2.5s | Web Vitals |
| Cumulative Layout Shift | < 0.1 | Web Vitals |
| Total bundle size (web) | < 250kb gzipped | bundlewatch |
| Flutter app size (Android) | < 20MB | flutter build |

---

## 11. ACCESSIBILITY

- All interactive elements have accessible labels
- Colour contrast meets WCAG AA minimum (4.5:1 for text)
- All images have meaningful alt text (or `alt=""` if decorative)
- Keyboard navigation works throughout
- Focus indicators are visible and styled (not removed)
- Screen reader testing is part of component completion

---

## 12. SEO & AEO

Full detail in `SEO_AEO.md`. Mandatory for all web projects:

- Every page has a unique, descriptive `<title>` (50–60 chars)
- Every page has a unique `<meta name="description">` (150–160 chars)
- Open Graph tags on all public pages
- `sitemap.xml` is generated and submitted
- `robots.txt` is explicit about what is and isn't crawlable
- Structured data (JSON-LD) on product, article, and organisation pages
- `llms.txt` is present at the root for AI crawler guidance

---

## 13. WEEKLY QUALITY RUN

Every Monday, the quality agent runs `docs/QUALITY_CHECKLIST.md`.
Findings are logged to `docs/TECH_DEBT.md` and a summary issue is created in GitHub.

Do not wait for the weekly run to fix a known issue. Fix it when you see it.
If you cannot fix it now, log it in `docs/TECH_DEBT.md` before moving on.

---

## 14. ADR (ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORDS)

Any significant technical decision must be recorded in `docs/adr/`.
Use the template at `docs/adr/ADR-000-template.md`.

A decision is "significant" if:
- It affects more than one part of the system
- It would be hard to reverse
- A future developer (or agent) might wonder why it was done this way
- It involves a security, performance, or cost trade-off

## 15. SCRATCHPAD AND DAILY LEARNINGS

This project uses the Two-Bible learning pipeline. See `docs/scratchpad/README.md`
for the full explanation.

**As an agent, your responsibilities:**

Before starting any task:
- Check if `docs/scratchpad/DAILY.md` exists and was modified today or yesterday
- If yes: read it. Apply any `rule`-maturity findings to your current task.

When the human uses closing signals ("wrap up", "what's next", "did we forget
anything", "safely deploy", "are we done"):
- Complete your primary response first
- Then add: "Shall I also write a scratchpad entry for this session?"
- Never write to the scratchpad without explicit instruction

You do NOT:
- Automatically write scratchpad entries
- Modify `DAILY.md` — only `/scratchpad:summary` does this
- Promote anything to the Public Bible — only `/scratchpad:export` and `/bible:update` do this

---

## 16. ASKING FOR HELP

If you are blocked, uncertain, or about to do something irreversible:

1. State what you are trying to accomplish
2. State what you've tried
3. State what options you see
4. Ask for guidance

Do not proceed with a guess on anything in the NEVER DO LIST.
Do not proceed on destructive operations without explicit confirmation.
Do not proceed if you cannot verify which environment you are in.
